ctx.x: Yeah. Those were the guys that I liked at the time.
This is wonderful. Jimmy Knepper, uhh, Michael Mantler, Howard Johnson, Steve Swallow, and of course Bob.
It isn’t that that’s incorrect, your information. It’s just that I played piano and organ on that probably and I probably also played chains and glockenspiel and anything else that was necessary.

items.title: Howard Johnson interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 14, 2019
items.q: But at this jam session was Roland Kirk, Carla Bley, who started using the tuba for everything shortly after that, Paul Bley was there too.

ctx.x: I did not know that. That’s awful. So you moved to New York, how do you find your way into the music community as a newcomer?

I had to find out what I had to find out. I didn’t want to be denied the opportunity just cause I didn’t show up. So there was no question of am I going to make it or, I just had to do what I had to do which was place myself in the right place. I didn’t have a tuba when I came to New York. I brought my baritone sax and I looked for an opportunity to get a tuba. When I finally got one I went — I hadn’t played in five years but I went the next day to a jam session place, back in the days when people who could play…
So I guess you made a good impression.
